reading.body:
Accelera Data Systems is not a confirmed data center, and the address attached to its name belongs to an unrelated garage door company.

The entry rests on a single OpenStreetMap node in Deer Valley, north Phoenix, tagged as a data center. Reverse geocoding that node returns A1 Garage Door Service at 2501 West Behrend Drive. No operator website, business registration, or press coverage for Accelera Data Systems could be found, and the name is generic enough that it does not describe a colocation or hosting business on its own. The likeliest explanations are a stale or imprecise map pin, or a tenant that has since vacated.

This matters for AI infrastructure counts because map tags are one of the few public signals for where compute sits, and a tag is not a building. A row like this can inflate a facility tally without adding a single megawatt. The site carries no published power figure, so it cannot be compared against Arizona's four facilities with published capacity totaling 512 MW, and it sits 15 to 20 miles from the other rows in its batch, so no shared campus connects them.

What the data does not establish is that nothing was ever built here. It records an exhausted search, not a demolition. The absence of a website, a registration, and coverage is evidence of absence of confirmation, and the coordinates alone cannot distinguish a mislabeled pin from a closed operation.
